judgments.title: SIM SWEE HARN & ors v LIM SEONG KEN
judgments.catchwords: 1. The late Sim Bee Tuan (“the Deceased”) was, by all accounts, a well-known eu char koay seller. The later years of his life, however, were marked by declining health and personal hardship, during which he took up residence in a temple, where he came to be under the care of those who managed its affairs. 2. Against that backdrop, the present dispute over his estate arises. By a will now impugned, the Deceased bequeathed the entirety of his estate to the Defendant, who was at the material time a caretaker and manager of the said temple, to the complete exclusion of his immediate family. The Plaintiffs, being the children and issue of the Deceased, have commenced these proceedings to challenge the validity of that will. 3. The stakes for the parties are considerable. If the impugned will is upheld, the Defendant stands to inherit the whole of the Deceased’s estate, leaving nothing for the Plaintiffs. Conversely, if the will is found to be invalid, the estate will fall to be distributed in accordance with the rules of intestacy, under which the Plaintiffs stand to benefit. 4. It therefore falls upon this Court to determine the validity of the impugned will. That determination must be made by careful reference to the evidence adduced and the applicable principles of law, to which this Court now turns.
judgments.judge: YA Dr Choong Yeow Choy

judgments.title: PERUNDING IRZI SDN BHD v MOHAMMAD KHAIRUL AIDI BIN JAMALUDIN
judgments.catchwords: Kontrak — Pinjaman persahabatan — Dakwaan bayaran yuran pengajian sebagai pinjaman — Ketiadaan perjanjian bertulis — Ketiadaan terma pembayaran balik yang jelas — Ketiadaan tarikh pembayaran balik — Ketiadaan komunikasi kontemporari menunjukkan persetujuan Defendan untuk membayar balik — Sama ada bayaran yuran pengajian UTM berjumlah RM28,028.00 merupakan pinjaman — Beban pembuktian ke atas Plaintif — Tuntutan ditolak. Keterangan — Penilaian dokumen pembayaran — Resit dan rekod bayaran membuktikan pembayaran dibuat — Sama ada dokumen pembayaran dengan sendirinya membuktikan sifat transaksi sebagai pinjaman — Hubungan peribadi, akademik dan kerja antara pihak-pihak — Pembayaran turut dibuat bagi manfaat individu lain tanpa tuntutan bayaran balik — Keraguan terhadap dakwaan pinjaman lisan. Restitusi — Pengayaan tidak adil — Projek Chuping — Pembayaran RM150,000.00 kepada atau untuk manfaat Defendan — Defendan mendakwa telah melakukan kerja-kerja projek — Penglibatan tertentu tidak semestinya membuktikan hak untuk mengekalkan keseluruhan bayaran — Tiada pelantikan rasmi sebagai perunding atau sub-perunding — Tiada kadar bayaran dipersetujui — Tiada peratusan dimuktamadkan — Tiada invois — Tiada penilaian bebas atau bukti nilai pasaran kerja — Pemegangan wang tanpa asas kontrak atau undang-undang yang sah — Tuntutan Plaintif dibenarkan. Quantum meruit — Seksyen 71 Akta Kontrak 1950 — Pampasan munasabah — Kerja dilakukan untuk pihak lain — Manfaat diterima — Keperluan membuktikan kerja, manfaat dan nilai munasabah — Seksyen 71 bukan lesen untuk mengekalkan bayaran tanpa pembuktian nilai kerja dan asas pengiraan yang boleh dipercayai. Tuntutan balas — Bayaran kerja-kerja Projek Chuping, Projek Pasir Raja, Projek Dendong dan Projek Sarawak-Sabah Link Road — Tiada pelantikan rasmi — Tiada letter of award — Tiada kontrak sub-perunding — Tiada surat arahan kerja rasmi — Tiada kadar bayaran dipersetujui — Tiada invois — Asas pengiraan tidak memuaskan — Tuntutan berjuta-juta ringgit tidak dibuktikan — Tuntutan balas ditolak. Profesion kejuruteraan — Skala Yuran Board of Engineers Malaysia — Defendan bukan Jurutera Profesional dengan Sijil Amalan — Defendan bukan firma perunding kejuruteraan berdaftar — Graduate Engineer boleh melakukan kerja teknikal tertentu di bawah penyeliaan tetapi tidak boleh menyamakan kedudukan dengan perunding rasmi projek — Tuntutan yuran perunding profesional tidak dibuktikan. Gantirugi — Gantirugi am dan gantirugi teladan — Tidak dibuktikan secara berasingan — Tuntutan utama yang berjaya hanya tuntutan wang tertentu bagi Projek Chuping — Gantirugi am dan teladan ditolak. Kos — Plaintif berjaya sebahagian — Tuntutan yuran pengajian ditolak — Tuntutan Projek Chuping dibenarkan — Tuntutan balas Defendan ditolak — Kos RM10,000.00 kepada Plaintif.

judgments.title: ALLIANCE BANK MALAYSIA BERHAD v BENDEN PRODUCTION SDN. BHD.
judgments.catchwords: Keywords: Originating Summons (Enclosure 1) – Plaintiff’s application for an order for sale under Section 256 and Section 257 of the National Land Code 1965 (the NLC) – legal relationship existed – the statutory requirements for foreclosure were met – the Defendant is the registered proprietor of the 14 subject lands – the Defendant admitted taking the loans facilities from the Plaintiff – security for these loans, the Defendant executed 14 separate instruments of charge (the Land Chargers) duly registered with the land registry – Defendant admits the creation of Land Chargers over the subject Lands – Defendant defaulted on the repayments of these loans – Plaintiff issued and served the requisite statutory notices in Form 16D of the NLC – the Defendant one month to remedy the default, which the Defendant failed – Section 256(3) of the NLC, the Court is obliged to grant an Order for Sale unless the chargor can show “cause to the contrary” – strictly limited to three categories – charge is defeasible under s. 340 NLC – chargee failed to meet conditions precedent; or the grant would be contrary to a rule of law or equity – Defendant failed to establish any of these limbs – the Defendant claimed non-receipt of the Form 16D notices at their registered address – Plaintiff provided evidence of delivery – postal authority via “Kiriman Banyak Barang-Barang Berdaftar – Court accepts this as valid service based on the deeming provisions in the charge agreement – service is effected upon posting – Defendant disputed the accuracy of the statement of account and the interest rates applied – the Defendant provided only a “bare denial” and failed to specify how the calculations were wrong or provide evidence of a “manifest error” – Defendant’s broad assertion that the order would be contrary to the principles of equity was insufficient – A mere allegation of breach of contract or dissatisfaction with loan terms does not defeat the registered rights of a chargee to an order for sale – Plaintiff has complied with all procedural and statutory requirements – Defendant has failed to demonstrate a valid “cause to the contrary” within the narrow scope defined by the law – Court is duty bound to grant the Order for Sale as prayed for in the Originating Summons.
judgments.judge: YA Datin Zalita binti Dato' Zaidan

judgments.title: Vinothmani A/L Ramani v Everise Shield Sdn. Bhd.
judgments.catchwords: Civil appeal - filed by the Appellant/Defendant against the decision of the Sessions Court Judge which allowed the Respondent/Plaintiff's claim with costs. Contract in business - in actions for goods sold and delivered, the delivery orders and invoices issued in the ordinary course of business collectively constitute a binding contract between the parties Part B documents - classifying the delivery order, invoice and statutory declaration under Part B of the Bundle of Documents carries a definitive legal effect i.e. the authenticity and physical existence of these documents are deemed admitted and remain undeniable - while their underlying truth or contents may still be subject to dispute, the Appellant is effectively precluded from challenging the genuineness, execution, or origination of the documents themselves - the issue of the authenticity of the signatures on the delivery order, invoice and statutory declaration raised by the Appellant is entirely a non-starter - by consenting to the inclusion of these documents within Part B, the Appellant has waived any right to contest their execution, rendering any subsequent challenge to the signatures procedurally incompetent. Burden of proof - the statutory onus rests upon the Appellant to prove the positive assertion that the transaction was an illegal sham - as the Appellant seeks to invalidate the contract by invoking the protections of the Moneylenders Act 1951, he must independently discharge the evidentiary burden to prove the existence of that illicit relationship.
judgments.judge: YA Dato' Sri Shamsulbahri bin Haji Ibrahim

judgments.title: SIVACHANDRAN A/L S JAYARAJAH v Pendakwa Raya
judgments.catchwords: Review jurisdiction - Rule 137 of the Rules of the Federal Court 1995 -Inherent powers of Federal Court – All sentences passed to be in accordance with the law – Avoiding miscarriage of justice - Exceptional circumstances - Fresh evidence of prisoner’s death following whipping. Constitutional Law - Federal Constitution - Articles 5(1), 8(1) and 8(2) Fundamental liberties - Life and personal liberty - Human dignity - Equal protection of the law - Whether it is in violation of medical ethics for medical officer to be participate in the execution of whipping. Judicial whipping - Corporal punishment - Whether judicial whipping amounts to cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment (“CIDT”) - Whether punishment of whipping is inconsistent with constitutional protection of life, dignity and bodily integrity. Whether whipping is disproportionate and therefore contrary to Article 8(1) - Whether exemption of women from whipping constitutes prohibited discrimination on ground only of gender is contrary to Art 8(2) - Intelligible differentia. Whether whipping is against Art. 5 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (“UDHR”) and the ASEAN Human Rights Declaration in its prohibitions against CIDT - Whether whipping is against customary international law.
